recommendations: Treat auth-service as NOT YET IMPLEMENTED in every downstream Phase 6 output. It issues no tokens: AuthController.java:34 returns the literal string "token". Any documented claim that the platform has OAuth2/JWT authentication is currently false at the auth-service end.

Decide one token mechanism before writing any code. Mechanism A (jjwt HS512 + jwt.secret, shared symmetric key with gateway-service) and Mechanism B (Spring Authorization Server + RSA JWKSource + /oauth2/jwks) are both scaffolded and both dead; keeping both scaffoldings guarantees a future split-brain.

Do NOT re-enable spring-security-oauth2-authorization-server 1.0.0 on Boot 2.7.5. Verify with 'mvn -pl auth-service dependency:tree -Dincludes=*oauth2-authorization-server*' after uncommenting pom.xml:24-28; the 1.0.x line targets Spring Security 6 / Boot 3 (jakarta.*), while every live import in this module is javax.* - see research question (a).
Fix the immediate compile break first: either restore spring-boot-starter-security (pom.xml:36-39) or delete the live imports at util/PasswordConfig.java:5-6. Everything else is blocked behind it.

Delete dead code rather than commenting it out, and drop the mapstruct-processor annotation path (pom.xml:127-131) until a real @Mapper exists.

Rotate and externalise the credential at application.yml:21 (jwt.secret default value - not copied here) before this repo is shared further; the file itself already carries the 'should be encrypted' warning at line 19.

Add Spring Security's AuthenticationException (or a domain exception) to the two classes in exception/ - extending javax.naming.AuthenticationException (JNDI) is a tutorial artifact, not an intentional choice.
